collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 4-9)

collection.description: A child begs an adult to ask a seal for the ride from the adult's old story: ask the seal politely, or tell the truth.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has told (friend) many times about the seal that once gave (subject.him/her) a ride all the way round the bay, while (subject) held onto its neck and the waves splashed past. Today a seal is lying on the rocks in the sun, and (friend) is tugging at (subject)'s arm. "Ask it for a ride!"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) walks a little closer and says, very politely, "Would you give us a ride?" The seal opens one eye, looks at (subject) for a long moment, and rolls over with its back to them. "It's tired," (subject) explains. "It's had a busy morning." (friend) accepts this completely, and they tiptoe away so as not to disturb it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "The truth is," says (subject), crouching down, "I swam next to one. Just next to it, for a little while. It was the best swim I ever had." (friend) thinks about this. "That's still good," (friend.he/she) decides. They sit and watch the seal sleep, and it turns out to be quite enough.
